name: Brineworks Salvage Hauler's Full Kit
description: A working outfit engineered for physical labor in the reclaimed industrial waterfront zones, where salt-brine flooding combines with acid rain and heavy lifting to destroy ordinary clothing in weeks. The foundation is a compression base layer in rust-orange thermal knit — the color is original, not faded, sourced from a medical supply surplus lot and repurposed, the fabric designed for moisture-wicking and now doing double duty as thermal insulation. Over it: a sleeveless work vest in heavy waxed canvas, originally dark green but now a mottled, oil-stained near-black, with six external pockets of varying sizes and a single interior chest pocket sealed with a metal clasp salvaged from a corponation document case. The vest's back is wide and unobstructed, gene-compatible: two long diagonal slits have been cleanly cut and re-hemmed with reinforced binding tape, accommodating a pair of vestigial decorative wings — the geneware kind, too small for flight but real feather and bone, here folded tight against the back in dusty gray-brown. Work trousers are canvas duck cloth in stained khaki, the legs tucked into knee-high rubber wading boots in matte black, the kind used in chemical processing facilities, with the original corponation logo scrubbed off and replaced with a hand-scratched personal mark. A wide oilskin apron is tied over the trousers from waist to knee, spattered with brine residue and chemical staining. Hands are covered in heavy rubberized work gloves, one thumb heavily wrapped in self-repair tape over what is clearly a healed-badly fracture. A battered wide-face respirator hangs around the neck on a strip of industrial webbing, ready to be pulled up.
functionality: Brine and acid-rain resistance through full rubber boot coverage and waxed/oilskin outer layers. Wide-back vest accommodates decorative wing geneware without restriction. Six external cargo pockets for tools and salvage. Apron provides splash protection for lower body. Respirator on quick-access webbing for sudden chemical exposure. Moisture-wicking base layer manages sweat during heavy labor.
what_it_says: A physical worker, someone who hauls and lifts and wades through things other people don't want to touch. The wings are a personal choice — geneware on the Shelf is rare and expensive, and decorative wings are even rarer, a statement of self that survives despite the circumstances. They weren't bought recently; they're old growth, lived-in. This person had a different life at some point, or saved for a very long time for something that makes them feel like themselves.
worn_by: scrap dealers working wet industrial zones
manufacturer: Medical surplus repurposed (base layer); remaining components from Shelf markets and chemical supply salvage
price_range: Φ20–Φ50 total; wings geneware separate and significantly more
story_hooks: The document-case clasp on the interior chest pocket is still engraved with a corponation seal — the clasp came with something inside it, and whatever that was, the wearer has never told anyone.

The wing accommodation cuts in the vest were made by someone who knew exactly what they were doing — precise, clean, professionally hemmed. On the Shelf, that level of tailoring skill is either a Tier 2 exile or someone who used to make a living doing it.

The personal mark scratched into the rubber boots matches a mark found on three pieces of salvage that turned up in a Tier 3 market this week — salvage that was reported as destroyed in a controlled demolition the corponation claims was routine.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutally practical salvage worker's ensemble built from medical surplus and scrap-market components. The silhouette is blocky and utilitarian—layered for chemical resistance and thermal protection, with functional bulk at the torso. The most striking feature: vestigial geneware wings folded against the back, visible through reinforced slits in the vest, adding an unsettling organic contrast to the industrial wear. The overall impression is someone who works in zones where ordinary fabric fails—seasoned, patched, and still functional.
physical_description.fit: Compression base layer hugs the torso; sleeveless vest sits loose and wide for mobility and heat dissipation. Trousers are relaxed and sturdy, tucked into boots for waterproofing. The apron drapes from waist to knee with slight sag from accumulated weight and moisture. Gloves are tight but creased from repeated use.
physical_description.primary_material: Rust-orange medical-grade compression knit (base layer); heavy waxed canvas, oil-darkened (vest); canvas duck cloth khaki (trousers); matte rubber (wading boots); oilskin fabric (apron); rubberized work gloves with textile palming; industrial webbing (respirator strap); reinforced binding tape (wing slits)
physical_description.texture: Base layer: smooth, moisture-wicking knit with subtle ribbing. Vest: waxy, slightly stiff, with deep stains that have darkened and hardened the fibers. Trousers and apron: rough canvas weave, heavily salt-crusted and chemically discolored. Boots: matte, grippy rubber with subtle wear marks. Gloves: textured rubberized surface, one thumb wrapped in self-repair tape creating visible ridging.
physical_description.color_scheme: Rust-orange base layer (bright, medical-supply origin); mottled dark olive-to-black waxed vest with irregular oil staining; faded khaki trousers with salt residue rings and chemical bleaching; matte black boots; cream-yellow oilskin apron darkened with brine and chemical splatter; dusty gray-brown wing feathers; industrial webbing in steel gray; self-repair tape in off-white.
physical_description.closures: Metal clasp (interior chest pocket, salvaged from corpo document case); friction-fit rubber boots with no visible closures; tied oilskin apron (cord closure); pull-on gloves; respirator hangs on webbing with no fastening.
distinctive_features: Reinforced wing-slits in vest back with binding tape, accommodating folded vestigial geneware wings (real feather and bone, gene-splice origin)
Six external pockets of varying sizes, all heavily used and stained
Salvaged metal clasp from a corporation document case repurposed for interior chest pocket
Heavy rubberized work gloves with one thumb wrapped in self-repair tape over a healed-badly fracture (visible damage beneath wrapping)
Hand-scratched personal mark on boots (original corpo logo scrubbed out)
Battered wide-face respirator hanging ready on industrial webbing, showing age and use
Salt-brine crust visible on trousers, apron, and boots—occupational weathering
Chemical discoloration patterns on oilskin apron (splatter stains, systematic wear zones)
Reinforced seams and tape repairs throughout, especially at stress points
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 (sub-grade/ungoverned). Every component is salvage, medical surplus, or scrap-market sourced. The outfit signals someone working in ungoverned or heavily degraded zones where corpo standards don't apply. The geneware wings—vestigial, decorative, and real—suggest informal body modification access, typical of sub-grade communities.
physical_description.cultural_context: A salvage hauler, chemical processor, or brine-zone reclaimer. Wearing this marks you as someone who works with hazardous materials in flooded industrial waterfronts, where ordinary clothing fails in weeks. The presence of real geneware wings (even non-functional ones) signals acceptance within a sub-grade community. This is not fashion; this is survival gear.
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily weathered and broken-in. The vest is darkened with years of oil and brine staining. The apron is actively stained, suggesting recent use. The glove wrapping is fresh but the glove itself is creased and worn. The boots show scrubbing marks where the logo was removed. All seams show reinforcement tape. This outfit is in continuous use, not storage—it's a working kit that will be worn tomorrow in the same conditions that created these stains.

image_prompt: A scarred, tired Tier 5 salvage worker in rust-orange compression base layer, sleeveless oil-darkened waxed canvas vest with reinforced back slits, standing in a flooded industrial waterfront warehouse. Vestigial geneware wings folded against their back, visible through the slits in dusty gray-brown feathers. Heavy khaki canvas trousers tucked into matte black rubber wading boots. Oilskin apron splattered with brine residue and chemical stains, draped from waist to knee. Rubberized work gloves, one thumb heavily wrapped in self-repair tape. Battered respirator hanging loose around the neck on gray industrial webbing. Moody blue-green overhead lighting casting shadows across oil-stained concrete and brackish water. Salt crust visible on all surfaces. Camera angle: full-body profile, slight tilt to show wing slits and weathered fabric details. Dark, utilitarian, working-class aesthetic. Industrial neo-noir scrapyard atmosphere. --ar 2:3 --v 6
